title: Dynamic array
statement: Start simple: Build a growable integer array with add, get, and size. Adding past capacity must preserve every existing value. Read the optional theory and C solution whenever you want a slower, more detailed explanation.
constraints: Start with a small backing array.
get rejects an index outside the logical size.
think: An array has fixed length, so growth needs a new array.
Copy the old values before continuing.
Track the logical size separately from the capacity.
Doubling makes occasional copies cheap across many additions.
hints: Keep an int array and a size field.
When size equals capacity, allocate a larger array and copy.
get must use size, not the backing length.

tests.name: one
tests.call: { DynamicArray a = new DynamicArray(); a.add(4); return a.size() + ":" + a.get(0); }

tests.name: order
tests.call: { DynamicArray a = new DynamicArray(); a.add(1); a.add(2); a.add(3); return a.get(0) + "," + a.get(1) + "," + a.get(2); }

tests.name: grows
tests.call: { DynamicArray a = new DynamicArray(); for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) a.add(i); return a.size() + ":" + a.get(19); }

tests.name: zero
tests.call: { DynamicArray a = new DynamicArray(); a.add(0); return String.valueOf(a.get(0)); }

tests.name: negative
tests.call: { DynamicArray a = new DynamicArray(); a.add(-5); a.add(8); return a.get(0) + ":" + a.get(1); }
